title: Portugal Fiscal Balance, 1977-2025: Reproducible Subsector Balance Analysis
description: This software archive contains a reproducible empirical research pipeline for decomposing Portugal's annual General Government net lending (+) / net borrowing (-), B.9 in national accounts, into Central Government, Regional and Local Government, and Social Security Funds for 1977-2025. The archived repository includes source parsers, harmonisation and validation code, analysis routines, executable notebooks, retained official source files, source-specific extracted CSV files, canonical processed panels, calculated analysis tables, generated figures, raw-file SHA-256 hashes, and the generated English report. The analysis is accounting, statistical and economic in scope; it does not infer intent, assign responsibility, or attach normative conclusions to fiscal outcomes.

creators.name: Ribeiro, Diogo

references: Banco de Portugal / INE long historical series workbook used for historical sector accounts, balances, transfers, GDP and labour-market variables.
INE data distributed through PORDATA, used as the continuous modern General Government B.9 bridge from 1995 through 2025.

Portuguese Public Finance Council (CFP) ESA 2010 annual workbooks, used for modern General Government and subsector accounts, revenue and expenditure components, interest, GFCF, Maastricht debt and stock-flow adjustments.
Portuguese Public Finance Council (CFP) Social Security report underlying data, used separately for internal Social Security budget-system diagnostics.
method: The pipeline extracts official source workbooks and CSV files into source-specific intermediate tables, constructs a canonical annual balance panel, validates the General Government subsector identity, preserves the known 1995 source overlap, and leaves the 1996-1999 detailed subsector account gap explicit rather than interpolating it. Derived outputs include year-to-year balance attribution, revenue and expenditure decomposition, sign persistence, transition probabilities, structural mean-shift summaries within separate statistical regimes, Social Security revenue and internal-system diagnostics, primary-balance reconstruction, fixed-capital-formation diagnostics, debt and stock-flow reconciliation, and descriptive nominal-GDP co-movement regressions with HAC standard errors. The final report is generated from persisted outputs rather than manually edited conclusions.
notes: Raw source files retain the rights and terms of their respective publishers. The MIT license applies to the repository code and accompanying original documentation. The checked-in outputs are intended for reproducibility and auditability. Detailed subsector revenue and expenditure components are not interpolated for 1996-1999. Social Security national-accounts balances and Social Security budget-system tables are kept separate because their accounting boundaries differ. Structural-break dates and regression coefficients are descriptive outputs, not causal estimates.
